explanation: For the corrected ln|x| equation, P=1/[x(x+1)] and Q=ln|x|/(x-9). Both are analytic at 3. At -1, P has a pole, but (x+1)P=1/x and (x+1)^2Q are analytic, so the point is regular singular. At 0, xP is analytic, but x^2Q=x^2ln|x|/(x-9) has an unbounded second derivative and no analytic extension, so the point is irregular singular. At 9, Q has a pole, but (x-9)P and (x-9)^2Q=(x-9)ln|x| are analytic, so the point is regular singular.
